chunks: And with this chain, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said: Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) said: Abdullah ibn Abbas used to say:
Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), when he ate a pomegranate, would not share it with anyone and would say: In each pomegranate is a seed from the seeds of Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about pomegranates and Paradise?
ai.summary: This tradition, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, links the Prophet’s personal etiquette (*adab*) of eating pomegranates alone to the spiritual potency of the fruit, which Abdullah ibn Abbas identified as containing a seed from Paradise. In Shia scholarly tradition, this highlights the concept of *barakah* (blessing) inherent in specific foods, suggesting that the Prophet’s solitary consumption was not out of selfishness but to fully absorb or preserve the unique spiritual energy of the 'Paradise seed' for himself.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-151 According to the same documentation, on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Husayn (a.s.), on the authority of Abu Abdullah Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) that Abdullah ibn Abbas narrated that God’s Prophet (S) said,
“Whenever God’s Prophet (S) had any pomegranates he (a.s.) would not share it with anyone and said, In each pomegranate there is a seed from Paradise.”
